title: SQL Injection in Login Form
description: The login endpoint at /rest/user/login is vulnerable to SQL injection via the email parameter. An attacker can bypass authentication by injecting SQL syntax into the email field.
impact: Complete authentication bypass. Attacker can log in as any user including admin. Full database access possible via UNION-based injection.
technical_analysis: The application passes the email parameter directly to a SQL query without parameterization. The backend uses sequelize ORM but raw queries are used for the login endpoint.
poc_description: Send a POST request to /rest/user/login with email set to a SQL injection payload
remediation_steps:
1. Use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation.
2. Replace the raw SQL query with Sequelize model methods.
3. Add input validation for email format.

code_locations.snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}' AND password = '${hash}'`)
code_locations.label: Vulnerable SQL query
code_locations.fix_before: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}' AND password = '${hash}'`)
code_locations.fix_after: models.sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = ? AND password = ?', { replacements: [req.body.email, hash], type: models.sequelize.QueryTypes.SELECT })
